authored: seed-example (hand-written template for the hourly task to match)
why_hard: Students confuse the many named angles/borders/processes on one flat bone.
The 3 surfaces (costal, posterior) and their fossae are hard to picture from 2D plates.
The glenoid's orientation and the coracoid/acromion relationship only 'click' in 3D.

three_d_plan.camera: auto-revolve ~0.006 rad/frame, drag to override; start posterior then rotate to lateral for the glenoid.

blueprint_plan.note: whole scapula revolving; label body, borders, angles
costal vs posterior surface (subscapular / supraspinous / infraspinous fossae)
coracoid process + recap of the 4 landmarks

narration_steps.narration_text: The scapula — your shoulder blade. A flat triangular bone on the back of the ribcage.
The raised ridge is the spine, ending sideways in the acromion.
Rotating to the side: the shallow glenoid cavity, where the arm bone sits.
The hook in front is the coracoid process, an anchor for muscles and ligaments.
